test_title: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-1 (Held On: 17 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The 91st Amendment Act, 2003 of the Indian Constitution is related with which of the following?

options.text: Limiting the size of the Council of Ministers
No enhancement of seats of Lok sabha and vidhan sabha til 2026
Bifurcation of the National commission of SC and ST
Fixed the strength of the Goa Legislative Assembly at a minimum of 30 members

solution:
The correct answer is __**Limiting the size of the Council of Ministers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **91st Amendment Act, 2003** of the Indian Constitution introduced a significant reform to limit the size of the Council of Ministers in the Union and State legislatures.
 
• The amendment added **Clause (1A) to Article 75** and **Clause (1A) to Article 164**, which set a cap on the size of the Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister or Chief Minister, to **15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha or State Legislative Assembly**, respectively.
 
• The act aimed to promote efficiency and reduce the burden on the exchequer by avoiding excessively large councils of ministers.
 
• It also introduced a provision under **Article 361B**, disqualifying defectors from holding public office or ministerial positions.
 
• This amendment was a part of electoral and political reforms to address issues like political instability and rampant defections.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Background:**

 
 
• The 91st Amendment Act was enacted in response to concerns over the growing size of the Council of Ministers and frequent defections, which were negatively impacting governance and stability.
 
• This amendment built upon earlier reforms initiated by the **52nd Amendment Act, 1985**, which introduced the Anti-Defection Law under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Key Provisions of the 91st Amendment:**
 
 
• **Article 75(1A):** Limits the size of the Union Council of Ministers to 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.
 
• **Article 164(1A):** Imposes a similar restriction on the size of the Council of Ministers in states, capping it at 15% of the strength of the State Legislative Assembly (with a minimum of 12 members).
 
• **Article 361B:** Disqualifies members disqualified under the Anti-Defection Law from holding ministerial positions or other remunerative political offices.
 
• The amendment also removed the earlier provision that allowed defectors to be reappointed as ministers.
 
 
 
• **Objective and Impact:**
 
 
• The primary goal was to curb political opportunism, promote political stability, and reduce unnecessary expenditure on oversized Councils of Ministers.
 
• It also reinforced accountability and improved governance by ensuring that ministerial appointments were more streamlined and purposeful.
 
 
 
• **Comparative Examples:**
 
 
• Before the amendment, several states and the Union government had excessively large councils of ministers, leading to inefficiency and high expenses.
 
• Post-amendment, governments were compelled to limit their Council of Ministers, promoting better resource allocation and administrative efficiency.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Options and Their Relevance:**

 
 
• **No enhancement of seats of Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha till 2026:** This relates to the **84th Amendment Act, 2001**, not the 91st Amendment.
 
• **Bifurcation of the National Commission for SC and ST:** This was addressed by the **89th Amendment Act, 2003**, which created separate commissions for Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST).
 
• **Fixed the strength of the Goa Legislative Assembly at 30 members:** This is unrelated to the 91st Amendment Act and pertains to provisions specific to Goa's legislative structure.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Anti-Defection Law:**
 
 
• It prevents legislators from switching parties for personal gain, promoting political stability and discipline.
 
• The 91st Amendment Act strengthened this law by introducing stricter disqualification provisions for defectors.
